characters.name: Jacopo Ortis
characters.description: A young Venetian who leaves his native city and retreats to the Euganean Hills. He is a young Italian patriot who struggles with political disillusionment, unrequited love, and a profound sense of despair. Disappointed by the loss of his country’s freedom and unable to be with the woman he loves, Teresa, Jacopo becomes increasingly isolated. His character embodies the Romantic ideals of passion, individual freedom, and the conflict between personal feelings and historical circumstances.

characters.name: Lorenzo Alderani
characters.role: Recipient of the letters; fictional editor
characters.description: Lorenzo Alderani is Jacopo Ortis’s closest friend and the recipient of his letters. After Jacopo’s death, Lorenzo collects and publishes his correspondence, providing the narrative framework of the novel. Although he is not the main protagonist, he plays a crucial role as the editor and mediator of Jacopo’s story, allowing readers to discover his thoughts, emotions, and inner struggles through his letters.

sections: Letters I, II, IV (addressed by name)

characters.name: Teresa
characters.description: Teresa is the young woman Jacopo Ortis falls deeply in love with. Although she reciprocates his feelings, she is engaged to Odoardo, a man chosen for her by her father. Torn between her love for Jacopo and her family obligations, Teresa embodies the conflict between personal desires and social conventions. Her relationship with Jacopo is central to the novel’s tragic development, intensifying his emotional suffering and sense of hopelessness.

characters.name: Odoardo
characters.description: Odoardo is Teresa’s fiancé, chosen by her father as a suitable husband. He represents rationality, social respectability, and the conventional values of the society in which the characters live. Unlike Jacopo, he is portrayed as controlled and pragmatic rather than passionate and impulsive. His engagement to Teresa becomes one of the main obstacles to Jacopo and Teresa’s love, contributing to the novel’s tragic development.

characters.name: Giovannina
characters.description: Teresa's little daughter, the only child left to her from her marriage.

characters.name: Signor T.
characters.description: Teresa's father, described by Lorenzo as a man of cultured mind and great honesty, whom he met in Padua. His name is abbreviated 'T***' in 1802 and 'T.' in 1817.

characters.name: Madre di Jacopo
characters.description: Jacopo's mother, never named, who is referred to as 'mia madre'. He leaves Venice for the Euganean Hills out of love for her, and her tears are what persuade him to go.

characters.name: Lauretta
characters.description: A young woman acquainted with Jacopo, grieving the death of Eugenio.

characters.name: Eugenio
characters.description: Lauretta's beloved, who died in her arms.

characters.name: Michele
characters.description: Jacopo's servant and messenger. In the Bolognese edition he carries the letters to the post office in Padua; in 1802 and 1817 he appears in letter IV.

characters.name: Plutarco
characters.role: Greek author whose works Jacopo reads
characters.description: Plutarch, the Greek author. Jacopo spends his mornings with 'il mio Plutarco' and reads him.

characters.name: Licurgo
characters.description: Lycurgus of Sparta, one of the ancient figures Jacopo reads aloud to the villagers.

characters.name: Timoleone
characters.description: Timoleon of Corinth, another of the ancient figures Jacopo reads aloud to the villagers.

characters.name: Dante
characters.description: Dante Alighieri is named as the author of an epigraph that appears only in one reading of the 1817 edition (witness Z), in letter I.
